c01-1: The letter of assignment gives his name and occupation. What is usually missing is a face: look for a photograph of a couple taken in a studio.
c01-2: Useful document: a Studio Lumen wedding cabinet card, dated 1870. The Reader returns it for the founder’s given name or for the name of the studio.
c01-3: Back of the wedding card: “Anselme & Clémence — 14 May 1870”. The man has a small scar through his eyebrow, the same one seen in the 1885 photograph at Les Tilleuls.
c02-1: The will calls her by her given name alone. Her birth name is in a Moulinvert register; her occupation is in the press coverage of the Grand Exhibition.
c02-2: Useful document: the Births of Moulinvert (1872–1879), found at the “Moulinvert” place on the map or by searching for the founder’s full name.
c02-3: Births register: “son of Anselme Varenque, papermaker, and of Clémence Aubertot, his wife”. Her occupation: the 1889 prize list mentions “Mrs Varenque, a distinguished botanist”.
c03-1: Two men share this name. This one died at the turn of the century and commanded ships.
c03-2: Useful document: the obituary in The Port-Sénane Echo (1902). Search for his full name.
c03-3: 1902: “Captain Firmin Varenque”, an engraving after a photograph: beard, gold ring. The 1873 marriage certificate describes him as “second master mariner”.
c04-1: “The keeper’s family”: the keeper may not be the person you assume. Look for the lighthouse’s service records.
c04-2: Useful document: the service records of the Tennok light (Lights and Beacons). Visit “Tennok” on the map or search for “Lights and Beacons”.
c04-3: Service records: “Mrs Maaren Varenque, née Tennok, 1883–1912”. In 1910, then, the keeper in post is the 58-year-old woman in the foreground of the postcard.
c05-1: Two men in the collection have exactly this name. Compare their ages, parents and faces before you fill in the slot.
c05-2: Useful document: an election poster from 1905. Search the Reader for the full name of Anselme’s eldest son.
c05-3: The poster “Vote Augustin Varenque” (1905): waxed moustache and pince-nez; the 1938 death certificate calls him “former Deputy”, aged 66. The other Augustin dies at twenty.
c06-1: She is often referred to by her husband’s name. Look for the charity she presided over.
c06-2: Useful document: the illustrated annual report of the Washerwomen’s Charity (1912).
c06-3: Photograph in the 1912 report: “Mrs Augustin Varenque, president, and our protégées”. Her birth name is on the 1897 marriage certificate: Henriette Sorbelle, the banker’s daughter.
c07-1: The will calls him “my brother”. His occupation rests on a famous poster; the 1906 trade directory confirms it.
c07-2: Useful document: the catalogue of the 1920 retrospective (Galerie de la Charte). Search for his full name or for the title of the poster.
c07-3: Catalogue cover: a self-portrait from 1910, pointed beard, the left eye drifting outward. The 1918 press calls him “the poster artist of The Washerwoman”; the directory, “poster painter, 12 rue des Tanneurs”.
c08-1: A birth certificate from 1906 names the mother but not the father. A poster idealises her face; you need to find it again in a real photograph.
c08-2: Useful document: Victor Sauge’s birth certificate (1906). Search for the given name of the child mentioned in Lucien’s letter.
c08-3: The 1906 certificate: “son of Pauline Sauge, laundress, 14 rue des Tanneurs; father not named”. The poster’s gap-toothed smile turns up again in the Charity photograph (1912). “Artist’s model” is not her occupation.
c10-1: The lighthouse postcard shows a man who is not the keeper. Look into rescue at sea.
c10-2: Useful document: the card “The Tennok lifeboat and its crew” (1912). Search for “lifeboat”.
c10-3: The 1912 card: “coxswain A. Varenque”; two fingers are missing from his left hand. The Tennok register names him Aldrik Varenque, “lifeboat coxswain”.
c11-1: Like Ostrian women, she kept her birth name. The postmark on a Tennok postcard bears it.
c11-2: Useful document: the photograph of the Tennok post office (1925). Search for her full name or for the name on the postmark.
c11-3: The 1925 photograph: “the postmistress Tenna Orrvik”, round spectacles, behind her counter. The Tennok register calls her “postmistress”. “Orrvikessa” is the same person.
c12-1: Only one man in the family is called “director” in the press. The newspapers of 1938 and 1953 print his photograph.
c12-2: Useful document: the Herald article on “the new grey booklet” (1938). Search for “grey booklets” or for his full name.
c12-3: The Herald, May 1938: “Mr Gaspard Varenque, Director of the Paper Mills”, round tortoiseshell spectacles, cleft chin. The 1971 obituary adds: director from 1925 to 1960.
c13-1: She is the bride of 1922. Her maiden name is on the marriage certificate and on the seating plan for the wedding banquet.
c13-2: Useful document: the programme of a recital at the Port-Sénane theatre (1928).
c13-3: The 1928 programme: “Recital by Irène Castagne, pianist”, with her portrait on the cover. She is the bride in the 1922 photograph (No. 2).
c14-1: She goes by three names in the collection: birth name, married name and stage name. A stage name is not an identity.
c14-2: Useful document: The Velmarche Eye, 1929, “… triumphs in The Lantern of Ostrie”. Search for the stage name printed on the Opera poster.
c14-3: The 1929 article describes the soprano as “née Varenque, daughter of the former Deputy”; a beauty spot above the lip. Her name is Blanche Varenque (Daubry is accepted), never “Aubertine”.
c15-1: He worked in two occupations; only one is what the documents after 1938 know him for.
c15-2: Useful document: the Herald article on “the new grey booklet” (1938), which photographs him with his brother-in-law.
c15-3: The Herald, 1938: “the Commissioner of Registers Marcel Daubry”. His 1923 marriage certificate calls him a bookkeeper: that is a decoy. Notched right ear, signet ring marked “D”.
c16-1: The press photographed her at her workbench in 1937. The Regency registers record her as dead: that does not stop you entering her.
c16-2: Useful document: the page “The paper trades” in The Velmarche Eye (1937). Search for “engraver” or for her full name.
c16-3: 1937: “Miss O. Varenque, watermark engraver, at the Moulinvert Paper Mills”; white forelock, a burn on the back of the right hand. Removal List No. 41 in the Bulletin of Order confirms it: “Varenque Odile, engraver”.
c17-1: His given name is in a letter, his surname on a removal list. A newsroom photograph shows him outside the restricted collections.
c17-2: Useful document: the photograph of the Vel Taalik newsroom (1936). Search for “Vel Taalik”.
c17-3: 1936: “the typesetter O. Kessvel”, next to Selda Varenque. List No. 41 reads “Kessvel Orrin, typesetter”: in the Reader, the restricted collection opens only to “Orrin Kessvel”.
c18-1: A famous aviator of the 1930s. His birth certificate does not name his father; the slot only asks for his name.
c18-2: Useful document: the press photograph of L’Hirondelle (1931). Search for “Aéro-Velmarche” or for his full name.
c18-3: 1931: “Victor Sauge and L’Hirondelle”, flying goggles pushed up, a slight squint. He claims to be the son of a captain lost at sea: the captain died in 1902, and Victor was born in 1906.
c19-1: Revealed through the aviator’s family. Her birth name appears only once, on the marriage certificate.
c19-2: Useful document: Victor Sauge’s marriage certificate (1934), found under his full name.
c19-3: The 1934 certificate: “Ninon Brial, costume maker”. At the Opera, in 1948, she is “Mrs Ninon Sauge, head costume maker”; turban and large hoop earrings in the Lac d’Aulne photograph.
c20-1: Three men in the family wear a gold ring in one ear. This one has a nickname, in Velmarchois and in Ostrian.
c20-2: Useful document: the photograph of an Ostrian wedding at Vellaak (1930). Search for his full name or for the bride’s given name.
c20-3: 1930: “Hessa Draavikessa ta Firmin Varenque — Vellaak”; clean-shaven at thirty. His son’s birth certificate calls him a “fishing skipper”. The Gull and Maask are his nicknames.
c21-1: She appears with her husband in a wedding photograph, and alone in an Ostrian newspaper, bag in hand.
c21-2: Useful document: the Vel Taalik article on “the women who welcome” (1936). Search for her given name.
c21-3: 1936: Hessa, with a leather bag, among “the midwives of the coast”. Tavik’s birth certificate names her “Hessa Draavik, midwife”; “Draavikessa” is the same person.
c22-1: The Regency struck her off for what she wrote. The Bulletin of Order and the Ostrian press both name her.
c22-2: Useful document: Removal List No. 3 in the Bulletin of Order (1938). Search for “the absent”.
c22-3: List No. 3: “Varenque Selda, editor of the banned sheet Vel Taalik”. Faces: the 1936 newsroom photograph and the Vellaak quay in 1953, freckles.
c23-1: A Deputy’s namesake. He dies at twenty; two documents from 1944, one official and one clandestine, show him.
c23-2: Useful document: a Regency notice posted in June 1944. Search for “Night of the Posters” or for the full name.
c23-3: Notice of 17 June 1944: “VARENQUE Augustin, aged 20, student”; an identity photograph, cleft chin. The 1924 births make him the son of Gaspard and Irène.
c24-1: He introduces himself in his letter of objection. He lacks a face: look for a wedding announced in the press.
c24-2: Useful document: “The wedding of the year”, The Velmarche Eye (1951). Search for his full name.
c24-3: 1951: “Maître Armand Varenque, barrister”, large ears, bow tie. He turns up again in the photograph of his father’s funeral (1971).
c25-1: A well-known voice from television. Her given name is in the letter of objection; her birth name in a wedding announcement in the press.
c25-2: Useful document: “The wedding of the year”, The Velmarche Eye (1951). Search for “RTV” or “announcer”.
c25-3: 1951: “Miss Mathilde Rouvière, the well-known RTV announcer”. The same face is on the cover of Velmarche Antenna in 1954.
c26-1: The letter of objection calls her “Dr”, under her married name. A directory gives her speciality.
c26-2: Useful document: a wedding announcement in The Orvelle Gazette (1956). Search for the groom’s full name.
c26-3: 1956: the wedding “of Dr Hélène Varenque, daughter of the Director of the Paper Mills, and Mr Paul Marsal”. The 1972 directory: “Marsal Hélène, doctor of medicine, paediatrician”.
c27-1: He wrote a series of articles on the papers of the Regency. Same occupation as another slot in the tree.
c27-2: Useful document: “The Regency Papers (3)”, The Aubrelieu Courier (1968).
c27-3: 1968: an article signed Paul Marsal, with his photograph (broken nose). The 1956 wedding announcement calls him a “journalist on the Courier”.
c28-1: She works at the Archives. Her official birth is a lie; her slot is placed by blood, not by adoption.
c28-2: Useful document: the class photograph of the girls’ high school at Bains-de-Mérande (1955). Search for her full name or for the place.
c28-3: 1955, second row: “Lise Daubry”, the white forelock plain to see. The inventory of the collection is signed “L. Daubry, conservator”. Same date of birth as P-4471: 3 March 1942.
c29-1: Revealed through the aviator’s family. One directory lists her as a plain “engineer”, as if she were a man: do not be misled.
c29-2: Useful document: the article on the aviator’s crash in the Corvins (1966), which shows the funeral.
c29-3: 1966: “his daughter Claude, a woman engineer”. She is the “Miss C. Sauge, woman engineer at the CVC” at the inauguration of the LX-2 Reader (1973), and the author of the Reader’s operating instructions.
c30-1: The last to keep the Tennok light. Same occupation as his great-grandmother.
c30-2: Useful document: the Vel Taalik article on “the last keeper of Tennok” (1972). Search for his full name.
c30-3: 1972: “Tavik Varenque, the last keeper of Tennok”, red beard and gold ring. The service records of the light: “Tavik Varenque 1950–1972”.
